fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Post the address visibly at the detached structure if it sits away from the main residence and street view.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow fire apparatus and emergency vehicles to reach both structures.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive so it does not narrow the travel width or reduce overhead clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Clear a path between the main residence and the detached structure wide enough for responders carrying equipment.
• Keep walkways free of stored materials so responders can move quickly between structures.
• Mark or identify the solar panel system location and main shutoff point in a visible location near the electrical meter or main entry for responding crews.
• Keep the open lawn area nearest the structures clear of equipment, debris, or stored materials that could block responder staging or movement.
• Thin dense vegetation between the structures and along the access drive to allow responders to see and move between areas without obstruction.
• Confirm that gates or barriers on the access drive can be opened quickly from the outside without a key.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the scattered clusters nearest to the structures to reduce the amount of continuous tree cover that could carry fire toward the buildings.
• Trim back any shrubs or low branches that are directly touching or within a few feet of the structure walls.
• Remove dead branches and dry plant material from the base of trees closest to the structures.
• Keep the ground beneath tree clusters clear of accumulated dead leaves, needles, and debris.
• Maintain the open terrain areas around the structures by preventing shrubs or small trees from establishing in those clearings.
• Separate any shrub groupings that are currently growing close together between the tree clusters and the structures.
• Keep low-hanging branches on trees near the structures trimmed up from the ground to reduce the path fire could take from ground-level plants into the tree canopy.
